enriched_description: Large wading bird measuring 120-145 cm in height with wingspan reaching 140-170 cm. Plumage ranges from pale pink to vivid scarlet depending on diet, with darker coloration on wings and tail. Neck is extremely elongated and S-curved, comprising approximately one-third of total body length. Bill is distinctive with downward-curving shape, deep black at tip transitioning to pale pink at base, adapted for filter-feeding. Legs are exceptionally long and bright pink to red with webbed feet. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry with compact torso contrasting elongated neck and legs. Wings display black primary feathers visible during flight. Flight posture features full neck extension. Juveniles display grey-white plumage developing pink coloration over 2-3 years. Weight ranges 2-4 kg.

Small heron measuring 55-76 cm in body length with wingspan reaching 95-100 cm. Adult plumage is uniform bluish-grey with darker slate-blue body and lighter grey neck and head. Bill is long, pointed, and two-toned: grey base with black tip, measuring 9-11 cm. Legs are long and greenish-yellow to grey, adapted for wading. Neck is long and S-curved, retracted in flight. Wings are broad with darker flight feathers creating subtle contrast. Juveniles display entirely white plumage with pale bill and legs, transitioning to blue-grey over first year. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry with slender profile. Weight ranges 0.3-0.5 kg. Feeding posture features slow stalking with neck extended.

Large wading bird measuring 85-100 cm in body length with wingspan reaching 130-155 cm. Plumage is entirely brilliant white with no contrasting coloration. Bill is long, straight, pointed, and yellow, measuring 12-15 cm. During breeding season, elongated ornamental plumes (aigrettes) extend from back and chest, creating flowing wispy appearance. Legs are long and black with yellow feet. Neck is long and S-curved, retracted during flight creating distinctive hunched profile. Wings are broad and entirely white with visible black legs trailing behind in flight. Eyes are yellow with pale lores (facial skin) turning greenish during breeding. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry with elegant slender proportions. Weight ranges 0.7-1.5 kg.

Compact heron measuring 50-75 cm in body length with wingspan reaching 85-110 cm. Plumage displays cryptic tawny-brown coloration with dark brown streaks and mottling providing camouflage in reed beds. Neck is thick and relatively short compared to other herons. Bill is long, straight, pointed, and yellowish-green with dark culmen. Legs are yellowish-green and moderately long. Body exhibits stocky proportions with broad wings and short tail. Distinctive dark brown stripe runs from eye down side of neck. When threatened, adopts upright freezing posture with bill pointed skyward, mimicking surrounding vegetation. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry. Weight ranges 0.5-1.5 kg. Nocturnal and crepuscular habits.

Large wading bird measuring 90-150 cm in body length with wingspan reaching 150-240 cm depending on species. Body exhibits tall, slender proportions with extremely long legs and elongated neck. Plumage varies by species: grey, white, or brown with contrasting black, white, or red facial and neck markings. Bill is long, straight, pointed, and grey to yellow. Legs are extremely long with hind toe elevated or absent. Neck is elongated and flexible, extended during flight unlike herons. Wings are broad and flat with elongated tertial feathers creating trailing appearance. Tail is short with elongated tertial plumes extending beyond. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry with upright posture. Weight ranges 2-12 kg. Known for elaborate courtship dances.

Medium-large wading bird measuring 58-71 cm in body length with wingspan reaching 95-105 cm. Plumage is dark brown with prominent white streaks and spots covering body, wings, and neck creating heavily mottled appearance. Bill is long, laterally compressed, and distinctly drooping (decurved) at tip, greyish-green with darker tip, specialized for extracting apple snails from shells. Legs are long and greyish-brown. Neck is moderately long with white streaking. Wings are broad with white spotting visible in flight. Tail is short and barred. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry with slightly hunched posture. Head is small relative to body with pale yellow eye. Weight ranges 0.8-1.1 kg. Distinctive loud wailing call carries long distances.

Medium-sized aquatic bird measuring 38-45 cm in body length with wingspan reaching 90-100 cm. Plumage is predominantly glossy purple-blue with metallic sheen, darker on head and neck, lighter on body. Red frontal shield extends from bill base onto forehead, contrasting with bright red bill tipped yellow. Legs are extremely long and yellowish-green with large unwebbed toes adapted for walking on floating vegetation. Wings display greenish iridescence in flight. Tail is short with white undertail coverts visible when raised. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry with laterally compressed profile for moving through dense vegetation. Neck is moderately long. Weight ranges 0.2-0.5 kg. Red and blue coloration is most vivid during breeding season.

Medium-sized aquatic bird measuring 34-43 cm in body length with wingspan reaching 55-60 cm. Plumage is uniformly dark slate-grey to black with lighter grey flanks. Most distinctive feature is bright white bill with dark brown to black frontal shield extending onto forehead. Eyes are bright red. Legs are greenish-yellow with unique lobed toes (not webbed) - each toe has flattened lobes that expand during swimming stroke and fold on recovery. Body exhibits rounded, duck-like profile with short neck and small head. Wings are broad with white leading edge visible in flight. Tail is short with white undertail coverts. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry. Weight ranges 0.4-0.6 kg. Runs across water surface before takeoff.

Large heavy-bodied terrestrial bird measuring 50-120 cm in body length with wingspan reaching 120-260 cm depending on species. Plumage displays cryptic brown, grey, and buff coloration with barred and mottled patterns providing camouflage in grassland habitats. Body is robust and stocky with long powerful legs adapted for running. Neck is long and thick. Bill is short, stout, and slightly curved, greyish-brown. Wings are broad and rounded with dark flight feathers contrasting lighter body. Tail is long and graduated. Male displays elaborate courtship plumage with elongated neck feathers and facial wattles. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry with ground-dwelling posture. Weight ranges 1-18 kg with extreme sexual dimorphism. Capable of powerful sustained flight despite heavy body.

Small shorebird measuring 22-25 cm in body length with wingspan reaching 50-57 cm. Breeding plumage displays striking pattern: chestnut-brown upperparts with black and white mottling, black breast band, white belly, and orange-red legs. Non-breeding plumage is duller grey-brown with faint mottling. Bill is short, wedge-shaped, and slightly upturned at tip, dark orange to black, specialized for flipping stones and debris. Legs are bright orange-red and relatively short. Wings are pointed with white wing bars visible in flight. Tail is short with white edges. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry with compact stocky profile. Head displays white eyebrow stripe and dark eye line. Weight ranges 90-140 grams. Distinctive feeding behavior of turning over stones with bill.
